name: comuneros-revolt-new-granada
description: Thousands of townspeople marched on Bogota against crushing colonial taxes, forcing a short-lived settlement with Spanish officials.

name: inconfidencia-mineira-plot
description: Brazilian miners, poets and a dentist nicknamed Tiradentes plotted to overthrow Portuguese rule before they were betrayed.

name: haitian-revolution-uprising-begins
description: Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose in a vast uprising that launched a long revolution.

name: narino-prints-rights-of-man
friendly_name: Narino Prints the Rights of Man
description: Antonio Narino secretly printed a Spanish translation of the French declaration of rights in Bogota and was jailed for it.

name: gual-espana-conspiracy
description: A plot centred on the port of La Guaira sought a republic with equality among races and was crushed by Spanish authorities.

name: toussaint-louverture-captured
description: French forces tricked and arrested the Haitian revolutionary leader and shipped him to a freezing fortress prison in France.

name: portuguese-court-reaches-brazil
description: Chased by Napoleon's army, the royal family reached Rio de Janeiro, turning a colony into the seat of an empire.

name: grito-de-dolores
description: A village priest named Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell and called his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule in Mexico.

name: bolivar-named-el-libertador
description: After the Admirable Campaign retook Caracas, Simon Bolivar was hailed with the title that would define him.

name: san-martin-crosses-andes
description: An army of Argentines and Chileans hauled artillery over high mountain passes to surprise the Spanish in Chile.

name: battle-of-boyaca
description: Bolivar's army surprised and defeated Spanish royalists in the Colombian highlands, opening the road to Bogota.

name: bolivar-dies-santa-marta
description: The Liberator died ill and embittered on the Colombian coast as his union of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador fell apart.

name: spain-recognizes-mexico
description: Madrid finally signed a treaty accepting Mexican independence after years of refusing to acknowledge its loss.

name: duarte-founds-la-trinitaria
description: Juan Pablo Duarte formed a secret society in Santo Domingo to win independence from Haitian rule.

name: dominican-independence-declared
description: Rebels seized a city gate in Santo Domingo and proclaimed their separation from Haiti, founding a new republic.

name: narciso-lopez-invades-cuba
description: A Venezuelan-born general led American volunteers to free Cuba from Spain but was captured and executed in Havana.

name: dominicans-rise-capotillo
description: Patriots raised their flag on a hill by the Haitian border to drive out Spain, which had retaken the country.

name: spain-leaves-santo-domingo
description: Spanish troops evacuated the Dominican Republic after a costly guerrilla war, ending the re-annexation.

name: grito-de-yara
description: Carlos Manuel de Cespedes freed his slaves and declared war on Spain, opening Cuba's first long war for independence.

name: virginius-affair
description: Spain executed dozens aboard a ship carrying arms to Cuban rebels, nearly provoking war with the United States.

name: protest-of-baragua
description: General Antonio Maceo refused to accept the peace that ended the Ten Years' War, vowing to keep fighting for Cuba.

name: marti-founds-cuban-revolutionary-party
description: Jose Marti united exiles in a party to organize a new war for Cuban and Puerto Rican independence.

name: grito-de-baire
description: A fresh uprising began across eastern Cuba, and Jose Marti landed soon after, only to die in battle within weeks.

name: antonio-maceo-killed
description: The Bronze Titan, Cuba's most feared rebel general, was killed near Havana, a heavy blow to the independence army.

name: treaty-paris-spain-cedes-colonies
friendly_name: Spain Loses Cuba and Puerto Rico
description: After a brief war with the United States, Spain ceded its last major American colonies by treaty.

name: cuba-becomes-republic
description: The American occupation ended and Tomas Estrada Palma took office as the first president of independent Cuba.
